capitals.name: Nouméa
capitals.note: Page: 'The capital of New Caledonia is Nouméa'; 'Captain Louis-Marie-François Tardy de Montravel founded Port-de-France (Nouméa) on 25 June 1854' (reviewer oc-02-a, 2026-10-18: from changed 1853 to 1854). The page does not say where the seat stood in 1853-1854.

keyframe_review.note: Mislabelled. The row's 1856-1858 shape (27,296 km2) is a multi-part French overseas aggregate: its bounding box runs 55 E to 168 E and 22 S to 23 N and lists India and France as well as New Caledonia, while the page gives New Caledonia 18,575 km2. Only its 53 cells on New Caledonia are the right land. Replace it by the island group from 1853 (new keyframe).

keyframe_review.note: Mislabelled: 93,627 km2 centred in Borneo (centroid 118.9 E, 1.3 N), touching Vietnam and France, five times the page's 18,575 km2. It is a French overseas aggregate, not New Caledonia; the real land is the island group. Replace it by the new keyframe.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1853-2024: the page's 'On 24 September 1853 ... Admiral Febvrier Despointes took formal possession of New Caledonia' (infobox 'Annexed by France: 24 September 1853'); area 18,575 km2 (infobox land area 18,275 km2). Natural Earth's country is used for the whole span; the page does not date the annexation of the Loyalty Islands or the Isle of Pines, so the first years may be smaller on Grande Terre alone.

region.text: Grande Terre, the Isle of Pines, the Loyalty Islands and the Belep archipelago ('the Loyalty Islands, the Chesterfield Islands, the Belep archipelago, the Isle of Pines')

ledger.note: 1853: France takes possession of New Caledonia. 'On 24 September 1853, under orders from Emperor Napoleon III, Admiral Febvrier Despointes took formal possession of New Caledonia'; infobox 'Annexed by France: 24 September 1853'. The page names the island group; dating of the dependencies is not on it.
1864: New Caledonia becomes a penal colony. 'New Caledonia became a penal colony in 1864'; about 22,000 convicts and political prisoners were sent between the 1860s and 1897.
1946: New Caledonia becomes an overseas territory of France. 'In 1946, New Caledonia became an overseas territory.'

1998: the Noumea Accord gives New Caledonia special status. 'New Caledonia was granted special status' (Nouméa Accord 'signed 5 May 1998'); it now 'forms a sui generis collectivity of the French Republic'. Referendums on independence on 4 November 2018, 4 October 2020 and 12 December 2021 kept it in France.

wars.name: Kanak revolt of 1878
wars.outcome: A guerrilla war led by High Chief Ataï of La Foa, 'a violent reaction in 1878'; the French colony stood.
wars.note: The page gives no territorial result and no end date; the rebels held no state of their own on any page opened.

wars.name: The Events (1984-1988 unrest)
wars.outcome: Violence between 1976 and 1988 ('the Events'), the Front Indépendantiste seized farms in March 1984, the Ouvéa cave hostage crisis in 1988; the Matignon Agreements of 26 June 1988 'ensured a decade of stability'.

certainty.note: An island group; the coast is the border. The Chesterfield Islands lie in the Coral Sea, far from the main island, and are not in the Natural Earth country.

sources.title: New Caledonia
sources.note: Annexation 24 September 1853, penal colony 1864, 1878 revolt, 1946 overseas territory, 1998 special status, area 18,575 km2, capital Nouméa, referendums 2018-2021.

notes:
Written 2026-10-18 from one page (budget 1-2). The Cliopatria row 'New Caledonia' (1856-1859) is not New Caledonia: both shapes are French overseas aggregates (bounding boxes from 55 E to 168 E and from 22 S to 23 N; India and France in the first, Vietnam in the second; centroid in Borneo in 1859). The real state, which Cliopatria lacks after 1859, is rebuilt here from 1853 to 2024. It may be that the aggregate duplicates rows that exist (french-india, french-indochina, french-africa); the colour agent and the France dossiers' authors should check. Type colony: drawn as a vassal tint of the metropole, so second-french-empire (1853-1870), french-third-republic, vichy-france (1940-1943: the General Council voted in June 1940 to reject the Vichy government, so the Vichy row should not hold New Caledonia), french-fourth-republic and french-fifth-republic should record the relation with counterpart new-caledonia, and not hold the land directly as well.

Not settled: the capital's history before today's Nouméa; the dating of the Loyalty Islands and Isle of Pines annexations (the page lists them as part of New Caledonia today); the Chesterfield Islands (Coral Sea), outside the Natural Earth country; the Free French years 1940-1945 (the page: June 1940 vote against Vichy; about 300 volunteers in 1941) change no border.
